details: Methods that mitigate overthinking in large reasoning models (keyword suppression, length penalties, binary early-exit) tend to induce the opposite failure, underthinking, hurting accuracy; the goal is to shorten reasoning without suppressing necessary exploration.

ReBalance: a training-free, plug-and-play inference-time steering method that uses stepwise decoding confidence and its short-window variance as a continuous indicator of overthinking (low confidence, high variance) vs. underthinking (high confidence, low variance).

Reasoning steps tagged as overthinking/underthinking on a small dataset are averaged into two hidden-state prototypes at a chosen layer; their normalized difference forms a single steering vector added to the hidden state of each reasoning step's first token.

A dynamic control function maps current (confidence, variance) to a signed steering weight: sign flips to push away from the nearer failure mode, magnitude uses a tanh soft saturation times a variance-gated amplitude whose mode boundaries are derived automatically from the model's own latent geometry.
Steering vector and control surface fitted once per backbone from 500 randomly sampled MATH problems, then frozen for all benchmarks.

Steps segmented by the \n\n delimiter; hidden state taken at the first token of each step; steering layer chosen automatically as the layer with highest linear-probe R^2 for predicting step confidence (PCA to 64 dims + ridge regression).

Confidence/variance thresholds set as empirical quantiles (q25/q75) of the extraction set; sliding window size |W|=2 by default; overthinking amplitudes derived from prototype-projection distances, underthinking amplitudes set as fixed fractions of prototype distance.
Four LRMs: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and 7B, Qwen3-14B, QwQ-32B; plus openPangu-Embedded-7B on Ascend 910B NPU.
Nine benchmarks: MATH-500, AIME24/25, AMC23, GSM8K, OlympiadBench (math); GPQA-Diamond (science); StrategyQA (commonsense); LiveCodeBench (code).
Metrics: Pass@1 and average generated token count; additional Pass@20 and Avg@4/Avg@16 multi-sample evaluations.
Early-exit / dynamic-stopping: DEER, Dynasor-CoT, FlashThink, TrimR (latter two reproduced).

Static fixed steering weight alpha_s (positive vs negative, magnitudes up to +/-3); univariate control g(c) or g(v) only; window size 2/5/10; underthinking boundary B_u in {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5}; steering layer depth sweep; gating function variants (sigmoid, linear, hard-step, polynomial, ReLU); extraction-set size and cross-domain/cross-difficulty extraction sources; decoding temperature 0.2-1.0.

Supporting analyses: Spearman correlation of confidence with response length, first-order Markov persistence of confidence states (Fisher exact tests), t-SNE/linear probing of confidence in hidden layers, overlap of prior methods' keyword lists with low-confidence tokens.

key_findings.finding: ReBalance simultaneously shortens reasoning and improves accuracy across model scales and benchmarks, unlike prior overthinking-mitigation baselines.
key_findings.evidence: On six math benchmarks and four models, Pass@1 improves by up to +10.0 points with token reductions of up to 35.4% versus the base model (e.g., R1-1.5B MATH-500 79.6->83.0 with -23.1% tokens; R1-7B AMC23 85.0->92.5 with -26.8%), whereas NoThinking/DEER/SEAL etc. cut tokens at the cost of accuracy.

key_findings.finding: Existing overthinking-mitigation methods induce underthinking, visible as a collapse of incorrect-answer lengths toward short outputs, which ReBalance avoids.
key_findings.evidence: Length-vs-reference-length distributions on MATH with R1-1.5B show prior methods shrink lengths for both correct and incorrect samples, while ReBalance shortens correct-sample lengths yet keeps the incorrect-sample length distribution similar to the original model.

key_findings.finding: Stepwise confidence is a reliable continuous indicator of reasoning state: high variance marks overthinking, persistently high confidence marks underthinking.
key_findings.evidence: Overthinking samples show higher confidence variance and underthinking samples persistently high confidence (Fig. 2b); across four models on MATH-500, Spearman rho between response length and minimum step confidence is -0.62 to -0.80 and with confidence variance +0.46 to +0.70 (all p<0.001).

key_findings.finding: Dynamic, bivariate (confidence and variance) modulation of the steering weight is essential; static or single-variable control only trades accuracy against length.
key_findings.evidence: With fixed alpha_s, positive values raise accuracy but inflate tokens (alpha=+3 on QwQ-32B increases tokens 147%) while negative values cut tokens and hurt accuracy; univariate variants g(c) or g(v) both degrade performance relative to the full g(c,v).

key_findings.finding: The confidence-derived steering direction generalizes across domains, difficulties, layers, and gating forms without retuning.
key_findings.evidence: Math-extracted vectors transfer to GPQA-D (+6.6 on Qwen3-14B, -22.4% tokens), LiveCodeBench and StrategyQA; steering at any tested mid-to-late layer reduces tokens without harming accuracy; five different gating functions give similar results; harder extraction sets yield accuracy-favoring surfaces and easier ones token-saving surfaces.
